208 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No major changes to the forecast. Revised information about the
ongoing precip event in the mountains.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Gusty winds will gradually taper off through tonight. Very
light snow showers may continue into tonight along the Tennessee

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Gusty winds will gradually taper off through
tonight. Very light snow showers may continue into tonight along
the Tennessee border. Trending warmer for the weekend.

Deep cutoff low will move NE through New England tonight. A trailing
shortwave concurrently will move thru the lower OH Valley. Abundant
boundary layer moisture is evidenced by the stratus or stratocu
field seen across most of KY/TN and the southern Appalachian
region. Low-level winds are west to west-southwest; though
that is not ideal for upslope precip generation along the TN/NC
border, light returns are seen on KMRX radar over East TN and
we occasionally continue to get reports of flurries in the NC
mountains. With the expanse of the upstream cloud cover and no
significant change in the sfc pressure gradient continuing to
provide brisk and gusty winds, think the flurries should remain
in a more or less steady state for several more hours. Light
accumulations mainly under 1" (but up to 2" in the most favored
spots) did occur this morning, but any additional accum is not
expected to be any more significant than that. Gusts of 25-30 mph
(and briefly higher) remain possible across the Piedmont through
sunset. Cloud cover should diminish after sunset particularly
east of the mountain spine. Slightly breezy winds continue into
Saturday though gusts probably not exceeding 20 mph.

Max temps Saturday return to near normal across the area, trending
a few degrees warmer for Sunday.


Key message 2: A cold front is expected to bring rain and more gusty
winds to our area Sunday into early Monday. After another quiet
period, another weather system could bring precipitation near the
end of next week.

Deepening shortwave existing the Rockies looks to induce
cyclogenesis over the southern Plains Saturday; the shortwave and
low continue to deepen as they swing across the MS Valley Sunday,
carrying a cold front across the Appalachians Sunday night. A stout
prefrontal 850mb jet of 50-60 kt is progged to precede the front,
with a decent Gulf connection suggesting some potential for heavy
rainfall Sunday afternoon and evening. Not too concerned for flood
potential giving the relatively short nature of the precip event
and with ensembles suggesting low probs of 2" even for a storm
total, and lack of a strong convective signal (though as higher
res guidance encompasses the event there's still time for that to
change). Afternoon and evening gusts again may exceed 30 mph in
lower elevations, and perhaps 40-45 mph on ridgetops, as we mix
into stronger winds associated with the jet.

Lapse rates from REFS, EC and GFS soundings are poor and there
does not appear much potential for SBCAPE to precede the front;
REFS ensemble max is less than 200 J/kg over N GA and our western
CWA by the end of the run 00z Monday; shear profiles are however
impressive and we would appear to have decent dynamic support from
the shortwave, so we will have to monitor forecast trends regarding
this system as a high-shear low-CAPE severe threat can't be ruled
out. The passage of the cold front does look to bring potential for
wraparound precip to change to light snow along the NC/TN border
early Monday, though significant accumulation looks unlikely at
this time. Following the front, cooler temps but dry temps can be
expected Monday and Tuesday before trending warmer again.

Most model guidance depicts another deep shortwave or closed
low transiting the Plains late next week. A few sources indicate
precipitation could start in our area as soon as Thursday night
on the warm side of that system; a cursory look at ensemble MSLP
fields suggest in-situ CAD could result, though presently it appears
precip would start as rain with anomalously warm temperatures
at onset. Confidence is low, but a slight-chance PoP is already
warranted Thursday night.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Upslope winds and moisture bring -SHSN to
the mountains along the NC/TN border, but those are not expected to
reach KAVL. Cloud bases remain largely between 020 and 040 across
the area at issuance time, due to moist layer beneath subsidence
inversion. Mixing is limited by the relatively low level of that
inversion, but drier air gradually should work into the area
through the afternoon and especially tonight.  KAND remains under
an MVFR cig early in the period; the other sites have improved
to VFR due to scattering and slight lifting, but where bases
remain below 030 a brief cig could recur through sunset. Where
this looked most likely a TEMPO was included. Winds remain gusty;
direction should continue to favor SW at all sites except KAVL;
gust potential begins to diminish over the afternoon though at least
low-end gusts could last into the wee hours of Sat morning. KAVL
is experiencing light/VRB due to mountain effects at the start
of the period, but should favor NW and see gusts develop by late
afternoon, continuing overnight. VFR, light breezy winds Saturday.

Outlook: Dry and VFR returns Saturday before a cold front brings
a brief shot of rain and associated restrictions Sunday afternoon
into Sunday night. Drier conditions return early next week.
